articles.title: Deputada Ana Júlia Ribeiro viraliza ao aparecer ao lado de Lula no discurso da vitória em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Aos 26 anos, ela ganhou projeção nacional em 2016, quando defendeu a ocupação de escolas durante protestos estudantis; agora, foi eleita deputada federal pelo PT com 184,6 mil votos.
articles.summary: Aos 26 anos, ela ganhou projeção nacional em 2016, quando defendeu a ocupação de escolas durante protestos estudantis; agora, foi eleita deputada federal pelo PT com 184,6 mil votos.
articles.body:
Deputada Ana Clara ficou ao lado de Janja, Janones, Rafael Fonteles e Alckmin — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A deputada federal eleita Ana Júlia Ribeiro (PT-PR), de 26 anos, viralizou nas redes sociais neste domingo (25) após aparecer ao lado do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) no palco do discurso da vitória, em São Paulo .

Durante todo o discurso, Ana Júlia ficou no pelotão da frente, ao lado do deputado federal André Janones, o general do "Exército do Lula", da primeira-dama Janja, do governador do Piauí, Rafael Fonteles, e do vice-presidente Geraldo Alckmin. Todas essas pessoas assumiram protagonismo na campanha de Lula e surgiu o questionamento de quem seria a menina "papagaio de pirata" do presidente.

Papagaio de pirata é uma expressão brasileira usada para descrever pessoas que se posicionam estrategicamente para aparecer durante transmissões ao vivo.

A parlamentar foi eleita neste ano para a Câmara dos Deputados com 184.691 votos , o equivalente a 2,96% dos votos válidos no Paraná.

A votação fez de Ana Júlia a deputada federal mais votada do PT no estado. A conquista também marca uma nova etapa na trajetória política da paranaense, que ganhou projeção nacional ainda na adolescência, durante o movimento estudantil de 2016.

Naquele ano, aos 16 anos, Ana Júlia se tornou um dos rostos mais conhecidos da mobilização de estudantes que ocuparam escolas em protesto contra medidas do governo federal na área da educação. Um discurso feito na Assembleia Legislativa do Paraná, em Curitiba, em defesa das ocupações, viralizou nas redes sociais e ganhou repercussão nacional.

Deputada federal Ana Júlia ao lado de Lula no discurso da vitória em SP — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert

A estudante Ana Júlia Ribeiro participa de audiência pública na Comissão de Direitos Humanos do Senado — Foto: Gustavo Garcia / G1

Na ocasião, a estudante criticou os deputados estaduais contrários ao movimento e afirmou que eles estavam com as “mãos sujas” com o sangue do adolescente Lucas Mota, morto em uma escola ocupada. A declaração foi dada durante a defesa da ocupação do Colégio Estadual Senador Alencar Guimarães, em Curitiba .

O episódio levou Ana Júlia ao Senado. Em outubro de 2016, ela participou de uma audiência pública na Comissão de Direitos Humanos para discutir os impactos da proposta de emenda à Constituição que estabelecia um teto para os gastos públicos federais nas duas décadas seguintes, conhecida como PEC do teto de gastos.

Durante a audiência, a então estudante criticou a proposta e afirmou que os parlamentares que votassem a favor do texto estariam “com as mãos sujas por 20 anos”. Ela também defendeu a continuidade da mobilização estudantil e a resistência pacífica às medidas contrárias ao movimento.

Na época, Ana Júlia foi comparada nas redes sociais à ativista paquistanesa Malala Yousafzai e recebeu aplausos durante a participação no Senado.

Da militância estudantil à Câmara dos Deputados

A deputada federal eleita Ana Júlia Ribeiro (PT-PR) ao lado de Lula — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Ana Júlia se filiou ao PT em 2018 e disputou sua primeira eleição em 2020, quando concorreu a uma vaga na Câmara Municipal de Curitiba, mas ficou na suplência.

Em 2024, voltou a disputar uma cadeira na Câmara e foi eleita aos 22 anos, tornando-se a vereadora mais jovem da cidade.

Neste ano, conquistou uma vaga na Câmara dos Deputados com 184.691 votos. Após o resultado, a parlamentar comemorou a votação nas redes sociais e agradeceu às pessoas que participaram da campanha. “É tempo de Ana Júlia na Câmara dos Deputados!!!”, escreveu.

Na publicação, ela afirmou que a campanha foi uma construção coletiva e agradeceu pela confiança recebida nas urnas. Também destacou a presença feminina na política: “É tempo de mulheres".

A estudante Ana Júlia Ribeiro concedeu entrevistas e tirou selfies ao participar de audiência pública na Comissão de Direitos Humanos do Senado — Foto: Gustavo Garcia / G1

articles.title: Amorim rebate Trump e diz que Meta que tentou fraudar eleição  | G1
articles.standfirst: Celso Amorim comentou declaração de Trump, que, sem apresentar provas, disse que eleição no Brasil 'pareceu fraudada'.
articles.summary: Celso Amorim rebate falas de Donald Trump sobre fraude nas eleições brasileiras e afirma que a Meta tentou obstruir o pleito restringindo conteúdos.
articles.body:
O ex-chanceler Celso Amorim , assessor de Lula para assuntos internacionais, classificou nesta segunda-feira (26) como "contraditória" a fala do presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , sobre o processo eleitoral brasileiro.

Para Amorim, Trump está "mal informado" e quem "tentou fraudar" as eleições brasileiras foi a empresa Meta , que controla as plataformas Instagram , Facebook e WhatsApp .

"Ele [Trump] está mal informado. Declaração contraditória, depois diz que gosta do Lula. Quem tentou fraudar a eleição foi a Meta, obstruindo e restringindo as nossas colocações. Só se ele está se referindo à Meta", afirmou Amorim ao g1 .

A campanha de Lula acionou a Justiça Eleitoral contra a Meta, acusando a empresa norte-americana de colocar barreiras a conteúdos do petista nas redes sociais a fim de favorecer Flávio Bolsonaro . A Meta nega interferências.

Mais cedo, nesta segunda, Trump foi questionado, nos Estados Unidos, sobre a derrota de Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) na corrida presidencial contra o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ), que foi reeleito.

Em resposta a jornalistas, o presidente norte-americano disse, sem apresentar indícios de irregularidades, que o pleito no Brasil "pareceu mais uma eleição fraudada".

Na sequência, ao ser questionado se faria algo a respeito, Trump afirmou que gosta de Lula.

“Eu não governo o Brasil. Eu governo os Estados Unidos. Gosto do Lula. Me dou muito bem com ele, mas a prorrogação concedida foi muito estranha.”

Lula derrotou Flávio na votação deste domingo (25), que ficou marcada pela primeira vez na história em que um candidato foi eleito após ter ficado em segundo lugar no primeiro turno.

O presidente obteve 51,79% dos votos válidos, enquanto Flávio ficou com 48,21%. O candidato derrotado do PL afirmou que não reconhece o resultado da votação e que recorrerá à Justiça para pedir a anulação do pleito.

Em pronunciamento após a derrota, Flávio contestou a decisão do ministro do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) Cristiano Zanin de prorrogar o horário de votação até as 19h em seções que ainda estavam abertas.

Segundo o senador, a medida teria comprometido a igualdade entre os eleitores e alterado as regras durante a eleição.

A medida de Zanin estendeu o horário de funcionamento das seções eleitorais até as 19h depois que ambas campanhas relataram dificuldades enfrentadas por eleitores em diferentes regiões do país.

A campanha de Lula argumentou que falhas no transporte público dificultaram o deslocamento de eleitores em diversos estados. O pedido encaminhado à Justiça Eleitoral citava problemas registrados em pelo menos nove unidades da Federação, incluindo São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Paraná e Pernambuco.

A equipe de Flávio também solicitou a ampliação do horário de votação, mas com foco em cidades afetadas por fortes chuvas. Os advogados do candidato alegaram que alagamentos, alterações em locais de votação e dificuldades de acesso às seções eleitorais comprometeram o exercício do voto em algumas regiões.

Na decisão, Zanin afirmou que a medida era necessária diante da gravidade das situações relatadas e da urgência do tema. Posteriormente, o ministro esclareceu que a extensão valeria apenas para locais onde as urnas ainda estavam abertas no momento da determinação judicial, descartando a reabertura de seções que já haviam encerrado a votação.

Apesar do tempo estendido para algumas seções, o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral afirma que apenas 35 mil pessoas votaram após às 17h. Lula registrou uma vantagem de 4,4 milhões sobre Flávio.

articles.title: Lula enfrentará Congresso à direita, crise no STF e precisará conciliar promessas com economia no 4º mandato | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente terá de ampliar o diálogo com o Centrão, negociar com um Congresso mais conservador e enfrentar desafios na economia e no Supremo Tribunal Federal.
articles.summary: Presidente terá de ampliar o diálogo com o Centrão, negociar com um Congresso mais conservador e enfrentar desafios na economia e no Supremo Tribunal Federal.
articles.body:
Reeleito para um quarto mandato, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) terá pela frente o desafio de governar com um Congresso com maioria da oposição, lidar com uma crise interna no Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) e conciliar promessas de campanha com equilíbrio fiscal.

A articulação política para aprovar propostas no Legislativo, a relação com o Judiciário e a condução da política econômica estarão entre os principais pontos de atenção de um novo ciclo do governo, que começa em janeiro de 2027.

Lula discursa na avenida Paulista — Foto: REUTERS

Na Câmara dos Deputados e no Senado, o fortalecimento do PL e a presença de partidos de direita devem exigir do Planalto novas negociações para formar maiorias.

No STF, Lula terá de lidar com divergências entre ministros em um momento de desgaste e questionamentos sobre a atuação da Corte.

Lula também terá de ampliar o diálogo com o Centrão, que não se sentiu plenamente contemplado na composição política do atual governo, e buscar apoio entre parlamentares que, mesmo pertencendo a partidos que apoiaram Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), optaram por Lula ou não seguiram a orientação das próprias legendas.

Na economia, o petista terá de conciliar as promessas de campanha com a necessidade de equilibrar as contas públicas e estimular o crescimento.

A dívida pública em alta, os juros elevados e a inflação resistente estão entre os desafios apontados por economistas para o quarto mandato.

O governo também precisará encontrar espaço no Orçamento para financiar programas sociais e novas medidas, em um cenário de desaceleração da atividade econômica e de pressão por um plano fiscal capaz de conter o avanço do endividamento ( veja detalhes abaixo ).

O quarto mandato de Lula começará com o desafio de negociar com um Congresso mais conservador e com o PL, partido de Flávio Bolsonaro, fortalecido nas duas Casas.

O PL t erá 121 deputados e 29 senadores a partir de 2027 . Ao mesmo tempo, o PT e os partidos aliados terão menos espaço no Congresso, o que obrigará Lula a buscar votos fora de sua base para aprovar propostas.

Esse apoio será especialmente importante entre os partidos de centro. PP, União Brasil, Republicanos, Podemos e Novo apoiaram Flávio Bolsonaro no segundo turno. Juntas, as cinco siglas somam 245 deputados e 51 senadores.

Isso não significa, porém, que esses parlamentares formarão automaticamente um bloco de oposição. A composição do Congresso aumenta a importância da negociação do governo com essas legendas para construir maiorias em votações.

O tamanho do desafio varia de acordo com a proposta. Na Câmara, por exemplo, um projeto de lei complementar precisa de 257 votos para ser aprovado.

Uma proposta de emenda à Constituição (PEC), que modifica a Constituição, exige ao menos 308 votos favoráveis. No Senado, são necessários, respectivamente, 41 e 49 votos.

No discurso após a vitória, Lula reconheceu que terá de negociar com o Congresso eleito, mas minimizou as dificuldades.

A relação com o Centrão, portanto, deverá ser um dos pontos centrais da articulação política do próximo governo.

Lula também terá de reconstruir pontes com partidos e lideranças que ficaram afastados do Planalto durante o atual mandato ou que não integraram formalmente sua base.

Outro fator importante será a definição do comando do próprio Congresso. As presidências da Câmara e do Senado serão disputadas em fevereiro de 2027, no início da nova legislatura.

Os atuais presidentes das duas Casas, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) e Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP), sinalizaram disposição para trabalhar com Lula após o resultado da eleição.

Motta afirmou que o presidente terá apoio para pautas voltadas a melhorar a vida da população. Alcolumbre disse que o Congresso terá uma atuação voltada à pacificação.

Motta e Alcolumbre articulam ainda a permanência à frente de suas respectivas Casas. O resultado dessas disputas será importante para o Planalto porque os presidentes da Câmara e do Senado têm poder para definir quais propostas entram na pauta de votação.

Ao mesmo tempo, o PL tenta ampliar seu espaço no comando do Congresso. Na Câmara, Motta buscou apoio de partidos do centro e da esquerda diante do crescimento da bancada do PL.

No Senado, Alcolumbre também articula sua reeleição, enquanto o PL indicou que pretende disputar o comando da Casa.

A composição dessas forças será uma das primeiras medidas da capacidade de Lula de construir uma base política para o novo mandato e avançar com sua agenda no Congresso.

Segundo o advogado especialista em Direito Constitucional Luiz Gustavo Cunha, o presidente reeleito precisará, nesse contexto, "demonstrar habilidade para negociar uma agenda legislativa sem transformar divergências políticas em crises institucionais".

"A utilização do Judiciário como instrumento para superar derrotas parlamentares pode até produzir resultados pontuais, mas tende a aprofundar o desgaste entre as instituições", pondera.

Outro desafio de Lula será lidar com a crise interna no Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), que vive um período de divergências entre ministros.

No próximo mandato, o presidente também deve quatro integrantes da Corte, o que pode influenciar a composição do tribunal e seu funcionamento nos próximos anos.

A previsão das quatro indicações considera a vaga aberta com a aposentadoria de Luís Roberto Barroso e as aposentadorias compulsórias previstas de Luiz Fux, em 2028, Cármen Lúcia, em 2029, e Gilmar Mendes, em 2030.

As escolhas terão de considerar o peso institucional do STF e o impacto político das indicações, em um cenário de tensão entre integrantes da própria Corte e de questionamentos sobre a atuação do Judiciário.

O racha no STF tem sido exposto por divergências entre ministros sobre a condução de investigações relacionadas ao Banco Master e sobre a divulgação de informações dos inquéritos.

A crise ganhou força no início de setembro , após a divulgação de um relatório da Polícia Federal (PF) sobre mensagens trocadas entre o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro , dono do extinto Banco Master, e o ministro Alexandre de Moraes.

Os desdobramentos das investigações levaram a decisões conflitantes de integrantes do Supremo e exigiram a intervenção do presidente da Corte, Edson Fachin.

Em meio à crise, Fachin defendeu uma resposta institucional aos fatos e afirmou que nenhuma autoridade está acima da Constituição.

Lula, por sua vez, defendeu que todos os envolvidos sejam investigados , "sem blindagem de ninguém", e passou a defender mudanças no Judiciário.

Na economia, um dos principais desafios do quarto mandato de Lula será conciliar as promessas feitas durante a campanha com a necessidade de equilibrar as contas públicas e manter o crescimento.

O novo governo começará em um cenário de dívida pública elevada, juros altos e pouco espaço disponível no Orçamento.

Economistas ouvidos pelo g1 avaliam que, sem um plano capaz de conter o avanço do endividamento, essas condições podem limitar o consumo das famílias e os investimentos das empresas.

Ao mesmo tempo, 90% dos R$ 2,8 trilhões previstos para as despesas primárias de 2027 já estão comprometidos com aposentadorias, salários, benefícios sociais e outros gastos obrigatórios.

Na prática, isso significa que sobra pouco espaço para despesas sobre as quais o governo tem maior liberdade de decisão, como investimentos e a criação ou ampliação de programas públicos.

Durante a campanha, Lula prometeu ampliar o Bolsa Família, oferecer transporte público gratuito aos fins de semana, manter a política de valorização do salário mínimo e aumentar os investimentos públicos.

As medidas podem sustentar a renda das famílias e estimular a atividade econômica. Mas, sem novas fontes de receita ou cortes em outras áreas, também podem aumentar a pressão sobre o Orçamento e a dívida pública.

A condução das contas públicas também influencia os juros. Quando investidores avaliam que a dívida pode continuar crescendo sem uma perspectiva clara de estabilização, podem exigir uma remuneração maior para financiar o governo.

Juros elevados encarecem empréstimos e financiamentos . Com isso, as famílias tendem a reduzir o consumo ou adiar compras de maior valor, enquanto empresas podem postergar investimentos. Esse movimento limita o crescimento da economia e a geração de renda.

A preocupação com a condução das contas públicas também se refletiu no mercado financeiro após a eleição.

Segundo Juliano de Lara Fernandes, da Armada Asset, o resultado das urnas e a perspectiva de manutenção dos juros elevados provocaram uma reavaliação dos ativos brasileiros.

“Essa queda de 16% do Ibovespa está diretamente relacionada à ruptura da expectativa de eleição de Flávio Bolsonaro, que vinha acompanhada de uma promessa de controle fiscal e queda dos juros”, afirmou.

Na avaliação do gestor, enquanto o novo governo não apresentar uma sinalização sobre a condução da política fiscal, a Bolsa poderá continuar refletindo a perspectiva de juros elevados, aumento dos custos das empresas e redução dos lucros.

A economista Tatiana Goes também afirma que o comportamento dos ativos nas próximas semanas dependerá das sinalizações do governo, das negociações com o Congresso, do cenário externo e, sobretudo, da credibilidade das medidas fiscais.

"Entre as principais dúvidas está a capacidade de compatibilizar compromissos de campanha, programas sociais e investimentos públicos com uma trajetória sustentável de dívida. Há argumentos econômicos favoráveis a políticas que sustentem renda, consumo e atividade; o desafio é definir fontes de financiamento, prioridades e regras previsíveis", afirma.

O desafio fiscal não apaga os resultados positivos registrados no terceiro mandato de Lula. A economia cresceu por três anos consecutivos, o desemprego atingiu mínimas históricas e a renda média do trabalho avançou.

A melhora, porém, não chegou da mesma maneira a todos os brasileiros. O custo de vida, o endividamento das famílias e os juros elevados continuaram pressionando o orçamento doméstico. Em julho de 2026, as famílias destinavam 28,7% da renda mensal ao pagamento de dívidas.

O desafio do quarto mandato será, portanto, sustentar o crescimento e financiar as políticas públicas sem alimentar um ciclo de aumento da dívida, manutenção dos juros elevados e perda de espaço para investimentos.

articles.title: Eleição 2026 tem 3ª disputa mais acirrada no 2º turno; veja histórico  | G1
articles.standfirst: Disputa entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro terminou com diferença de 3,6 pontos percentuais. Eleições de 2022 e 2014 foram ainda mais disputadas. No 1º turno de 2026, diferença de 1,8 ponto tinha sido a menor já registrada desde 1989 nessa etapa da eleição.
articles.summary: A eleição 2026 entre Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro teve a menor diferença no 1º turno e a 3ª maior proximidade no 2º turno desde a redemocratização no Brasil.
articles.body:
O segundo turno das eleições presidenciais de 2026 foi acirrado, mas não tanto quanto o de 2022 e o de 2014, mostra levantamento do g1 .

Na votação de domingo (25), Lula (PT) obteve 51,79% dos votos válidos, enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) alcançou 48,21%. A diferença entre os dois candidatos foi de 3,58 pontos percentuais e 4.430.191 votos.

Com esse resultado, o pleito de 2026 foi a terceira eleição presidencial mais apertada em segundo turno desde a redemocratização.

🔎 Desde a retomada das eleições diretas para presidente, em 1989, Fernando Henrique Cardoso foi o único presidente eleito em primeiro turno, em 1994 e 1998.

Até hoje, a menor diferença registrada na história em um segundo turno de eleição presidencial no Brasil foi no embate entre Lula e o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro (PL). Em 2022, Lula venceu o pai de Flávio por 50,9% a 49,1%: uma diferença de 1,8 ponto percentual e 2.139.645 votos.

Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Jair Bolsonaro (PL) disputam o segundo turno — Foto: EPA

Em segundo lugar está o segundo turno da eleição de 2014, em que Dilma Rousseff (PT) venceu Aécio Neves (PSDB) por 51,64% a 48,36%. No pleito, houve uma diferença de 3,28 pontos percentuais e 3.459.963 votos.

Aécio e Dilma se cumprimentam no início do debate — Foto: Silvia Izquierdo/AP

Veja abaixo como foi o segundo turno de eleições presidenciais desde 1989.

Diferença entre candidatos no 2º turno desde 1989. — Foto: g1

1º turno de 2026 teve a menor distância da história

Embora o segundo turno de 2026 tenha ficado em terceiro lugar entre os mais acirrados, o primeiro turno de 2026 teve a menor diferença entre o 1º e o 2º colocado no primeiro turno desde 1989 .

No 1º turno de 2026, a distância entre os dois primeiros colocados foi de apenas 1,87 ponto percentual — Flávio Bolsonaro ficou com 47,03% dos votos válidos, enquanto Lula obteve 45,16%. A diferença entre os candidatos foi de 2.224.965 votos.

O resultado da eleição de 2026 entrou para a história porque foi a primeira vez que um candidato que acabou atrás no primeiro turno conseguiu reverter o resultado e vencer no segundo turno.

Com a vitória, Lula se torna o primeiro presidente eleito quatro vezes pelo voto direto no Brasil. Aos 80 anos, o petista afirmou durante a campanha que esta seria sua última disputa presidencial. Pelas regras constitucionais atuais, ele não poderá concorrer a um novo mandato em 2030.

No primeiro discurso depois de ser reeleito, Lula dedicou a vitória inédita à "juventude rebelde que se levantou pela democracia", às mulheres e aos trabalhadores.

"Eu quero agradecer a cada homem, a cada mulher. Hoje, eu vi na televisão o gesto de muitos netos levando o avô e avó para votar em cadeira de roda. Eu devo essa vitória a juventude rebelde que se levantou em defesa da democracia. Eu devo essa vitória às mulheres que se rebelaram contra o feminicídio. Eu devo às pessoas que acreditam que o fim da escala 6 por 1 é um benefício pra sociedade brasileira. Eu devo essa vitória aos educadores que acreditam que a educação é a melhor solução para fazer o país falta de qualidade. Eu devo essa vitória a cada um e a cada uma de vocês", disse Lula.

Lula (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em agendas eleitorais na reta final da eleição — Foto: Ricardo Stuckert / Vitor Salles

articles.title: PRTB anuncia que passará a se chamar 'Brasileiro' e que construirá terceira via após vitória de Lula | G1
articles.standfirst: Partido reconheceu o resultado das urnas, cumprimentou o presidente eleito e afirmou que seguirá independente como 'oposição responsável'; legenda se manteve neutra no segundo turno.
articles.summary: Partido reconheceu o resultado das urnas, cumprimentou o presidente eleito e afirmou que seguirá independente como 'oposição responsável'; legenda se manteve neutra no segundo turno.
articles.body:
Leonardo Avalanche, presidente do PRTB — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal

O PRTB passará a se chamar Brasileiro, segundo nota divulgada nesta segunda-feira (26) pelo presidente nacional do partido, Leonardo Avalanche, após a vitória de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) na eleição presidencial.

A legenda, que se manteve neutra no segundo turno, reconheceu o resultado das urnas e afirmou que pretende construir uma terceira via conservadora, sem corrupção e comprometida com a soberania nacional.

“O PRTB, partido conservador que se manteve independente no segundo turno da eleição presidencial, reconhece o resultado das urnas e reafirma sua confiança na democracia e no sistema eleitoral brasileiro”, diz o comunicado.

Para Avalanche, o resultado confirma o que o partido apontou em uma carta aberta divulgada em 13 de outubro: “A pseudodireita apostou em dancinha nas redes e achou que isso bastava para convencer o povo. Não bastou. O povo brasileiro quer projetos e propostas reais, não populismo eleitoral. O eleitor acordou e entendeu que era seis por meia dúzia”.

Segundo o presidente nacional, a neutralidade no segundo turno foi uma decisão de princípio. O PRTB, de acordo com a nota, não se sujeita à “pseudodireita” e escolheu preservar sua independência para construir uma terceira via conservadora e sem corrupção.

“O povo quer alguém que se posicione, que seja contra a corrupção, que trabalhe pelo desenvolvimento e, principalmente, pela soberania do nosso país. É esse projeto que o PRTB vai construir.”

A legenda afirma que pretende apresentar nomes para futuras disputas eleitorais. “Vamos trazer grandes nomes para as disputas, mas com discernimento, com coerência, com firmeza e, principalmente, com clareza”, diz Avalanche.

O partido não antecipou possíveis candidatos. Segundo o comunicado, os próximos quatro anos serão dedicados à construção de uma terceira via que dê voz aos mais de 50 milhões de brasileiros que foram às urnas em busca de mudança e esperam alguém que defenda seus princípios.

A proposta também pretende alcançar eleitores que votaram no candidato eleito, segundo o partido, não por convicção, mas por não encontrarem na “pseudodireita” uma alternativa confiável. Para o PRTB, esse voto de protesto demonstra que o país espera uma opção política em que possa confiar.

“Esse é o nosso compromisso com o Brasil. A esperança vai renascer, e o Brasil vai conhecer, no tempo certo, quem vai representá-la”, conclui o presidente nacional.

De acordo com a nota, o partido quer unir o país em torno de uma política que debata ideias, respeite opiniões diferentes e não recorra ao discurso de ódio ou à humilhação de adversários.

“Nós vamos construir um candidato que represente todas as classes sociais de forma justa, sem corrupção, e que fale com todo brasileiro. Não é humilhando o próximo, nem com discurso de ódio que divide o país em uma polarização sem fim, que se constrói uma nação”, afirma Avalanche.

O presidente também declarou que a legenda não aceitará candidatos envolvidos em corrupção, independentemente do cargo que ocupem. "Quem quiser representar o PRTB precisa ter a ficha limpa e o compromisso com o país”, afirma.

articles.title: Após eleição de Lula, Centrão recalcula rota e admite compor com o governo | G1
articles.standfirst: Parlamentares que apoiaram Flávio reconhecem dificuldades do presidente eleito no Congresso, mas defendem negociação: ‘DNA pela governabilidade’.
articles.summary: Parlamentares que apoiaram Flávio reconhecem dificuldades do presidente eleito no Congresso, mas defendem negociação: ‘DNA pela governabilidade’.
articles.body:
O resultado das eleições, com a vitória do presidente Lula (PT) com mais de 4 milhões de votos à frente de Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) , surpreendeu a maior parte do Centrão. Na campanha de segundo turno, quase todos os partidos apoiaram o senador do PL, mas já recalculam rota menos de 24 horas após a abertura das urnas e admitem compor com o governo Lula .

O discurso é de que será preciso fazer um governo de coalizão, com a participação de outros partidos além da esquerda na Esplanada.

Como pano de fundo, há também o instinto de sobrevivência desses partidos, que temem perder espaço no Congresso diante do crescimento da bancada do P L. As cúpulas de partidos como Republicanos, MDB e PSD já conversam para tentar unificar a atuação do grupo após a eleição.

“Precisamos encontrar um caminho menos traumático para o país. O novo governo vai ter um cenário de antagonismo, mas eu espero que a gente consiga ir com maturidade”, afirma um senador do Centrão que apoiou Flávio durante a campanha.

Na mesma linha, o deputado Ricardo Barros (PP-PR) diz que Lula terá de negociar com esses partidos para garantir sustentabilidade no Congresso.

“Os partidos de Centro têm um DNA pela governabilidade, pelo compromisso de que o presidente eleito possa cumprir seu plano de governo, que foi aprovado nas urnas. Não vejo surpresa no que vai acontecer, que é a construção de uma maioria para sustentar o governo no nosso presidencialismo de coalizão”, afirma.

O deputado Ricardo Barros (PP-PR) defende que os partidos de centro possuem um 'DNA' da governabilidade — Foto: Bruno Spada/Câmara dos Deputados

Partidos como União Brasil, Republicanos – que apoiaram Flávio –, MDB e PSD emitiram nota após o resultado das eleições, parabenizando o presidente Lula pelo resultado.

“Reafirmo também nossa disposição de apoiar medidas e ações por um Brasil que cresça, gere empregos e reduza as desigualdades, em benefício de todos os brasileiros”, escreveu Antonio Rueda, presidente do União Brasil.

Em manifestação publicada nas redes sociais, o MDB diz que “é um momento em que a vontade popular se fez soberana”.

“Desejamos que ele tenha serenidade para governar o País em favor de TODOS sem exceção”, finaliza a nota do partido. Apesar de não fechar questão em favor de Flávio Bolsonaro, a maioria dos diretórios do MDB apoiou a eleição do senador do PL.

Já Gilberto Kassab, presidente do PSD, escreveu em nota de reconhecimento à eleição de Lula ter a certeza de que “nossos parlamentares e governadores eleitos seguirão defendendo os bons projetos e manterão a relação republicana com o Governo Federal, em defesa do objetivo comum a todos nós, que é o desenvolvimento do Brasil e o bem-estar da nossa população”.

Na base de Lula, alguns parlamentares concordam que o governo precisará fazer um mandato menos petista, sinalizando para os outros partidos.

Na avaliação de um ex-ministro, a nova gestão terá de ampliar o diálogo com setores da direita democrática , construir alianças e trabalhar desde já na elaboração do Orçamento de 2027, com propostas para ajustar as contas públicas.

Isso passaria por apresentar em até 30 dias um pacote com medidas de ajuste fiscal, em uma demonstração de disposição para construir uma agenda econômica capaz de reunir apoio para além de sua base tradicional.

Para este interlocutor, o gesto de Lula de permitir que o vice-presidente eleito, Geraldo Alckmin (PSB), fosse o primeiro a falar no discurso após a vitória foi um sinal de que o presidente entende a necessidade de ampliar a interlocução política e econômica.

O candidato à presidência do Brasil, Flávio Bolsonaro, do Partido Liberal (PL), discursa após perder o segundo turno das eleições presidenciais, em Brasília, Brasil, em 25 de outubro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Adriano Machado

“Péssimo para um perdedor começar o discurso dessa forma. Desmonta a moderação que ele próprio estava tentando construir, tirou a imagem que trazia para a gente de que ele não era o pai”, afirma um parlamentar do Centrão, em referência ao ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro.

Outro integrante do grupo também criticou a declaração. “Fala no calor do resultado. Espero que ele reavalie e faça uma fala mais tranquila”, afirma.

Alguns destes parlamentares lembram que o posicionamento vai contra o que ele próprio disse em diversas entrevistas, de que iria aceitar o resultado das eleições.

“É impossível reconhecer o resultado das eleições no contexto que essas coisas aconteceram. Nós vamos usar o nosso direito, vamos pedir a anulação dessas eleições”, disse.

O argumento do senador se baseia na decisão do ministro Cristiano Zanin, do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), de prorrogar por duas horas as eleições . A decisão aconteceu após relatos de estados que tiveram o transporte público afetado por falhas, redução de frotas e cobrança indevida, além de excesso de chuvas. Tanto a campanha de Lula quanto a de Flávio pediram a prorrogação.

A vitória de Lula também deve reconfigurar a disputa pelas presidências da Câmara dos Deputados e do Senado . Os atuais presidentes da Câmara e do Senado, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB) e Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP) respectivamente, foram aliados importantes do petista nos últimos meses.

Lula, Davi Alcolumbre e Hugo Motta — Foto: Foto: Ricardo Stuckert.

Na Câmara, a avaliação é que a reeleição de Motta está bem encaminhada. O deputado articulou um bloco com o maior número de partidos e isolou o PL nas negociações.

No Senado, a situação de Davi Alcolumbre é considerada menos consolidada devido ao tamanho da bancada eleita pela direita para assumir a partir de 2027. Apesar disso, o cenário com a vitória de Lula ficou mais favorável a Alcolumbre.

A avaliação é que o governo Lula deve ao presidente do Senado a aprovação de uma das principais bandeiras eleitorais da campanha: a aprovação do fim da escala 6x1.

Por isso e para evitar a chegada de um aliado de Flávio ao comando do Senado, senador Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), o Planalto deve se articular para garantir a reeleição de Alcolumbre.

Com o apoio do Executivo, Alcolumbre teria em mãos instrumentos importantes para negociar apoio dos senadores, como a liberação de emendas e a distribuição de cargos.

articles.title: Ramaswamy: Acton campaign ‘defamed my mother’ before attack ad
articles.summary: Republican Vivek Ramaswamy slammed opponent Democrat Amy Acton’s campaign on Sunday, saying her campaign “defamed my mother” before he released a controversial attack ad earlier this month. articles.body:
Republican Vivek Ramaswamy slammed opponent Democrat Amy Acton’s campaign on Sunday, saying her campaign “defamed my mother” before he released a controversial attack ad earlier this month.

Appearing on Fox News , Ramaswamy was asked whether he regretted releasing an attack ad that featured Acton’s estranged mother , Donna Arthur, calling her daughter a “liar.”

“I’ll tell you the advice I was raised in: You never start a fight, but if you find yourself in one, you finish it, and you have to stand for what is right and what is true,” he said. “They’ve attacked me. They’ve defamed my mother to media silence. It’s unbelievable. And yet, at the same time, they’ll trot out anything to attack a Republican.”

Ramaswamy did not mention a specific instance of alleged defamation. The Hill has reached out to his campaign for clarification and comment.

Acton has talked about experiencing physical and sexual abuse, along with neglect, during her childhood. Her mother stayed with her stepfather even after he was charged with sexually abusing Acton when she was 12 years old, according to court documents .

Acton’s campaign in August released attacks regarding Axovant, a company Ramaswamy founded that promoted Alzheimer’s medication, and the ad’s included his mother.

“Today, new reporting details how billionaire Vivek Ramaswamy hired his own mother, who lacked research experience, to manipulate clinical trial data in an alleged ‘pump and dump’ pharmaceutical scheme,” the press release read.

Addie Bullock, one of Acton’s communications directors, accused Ramaswamy of “shamelessly profiting off Alzheimer’s patients and getting his own mother to manipulate clinical trial data, to make a buck,” in a press release at that time.

Axovant went public and saw its value shoot up to more than $350 million in its initial public offering before plummeting after the company reported its Alzheimer’s drug failed Phase 3 testing.

An investigation by Politifact , a nonpartisan fact-checker, found that Acton’s claims concerning Ramaswamy pushing an “Alzheimer’s drug that he knew didn’t work” and making “hundreds of millions of dollars scamming people” were mostly false.

New polling from Fox News showed Acton leading Ramaswamy by 2 points, although her lead is within the poll’s margin of error of 2 percentage points.

articles.title: Ilhan Omar joins 'polarizing and dangerous' streamer at campaign event despite Democratic backlash
articles.summary: Rep. Ilhan Omar is set to share the stage with Hasan Piker despite fellow Minnesota Democrats urging her to cancel the appearance before midterm elections.
articles.body: Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., is set to share the stage with far-left streamer Hasan Piker on Monday night despite mounting opposition from fellow Minnesota Democrats, some of whom have publicly urged the congresswoman to cancel the appearance just eight days before the midterm elections. Rep. Angie Craig, D-Minn., has called Piker's rhetoric "polarizing and dangerous" and said embracing him is "a mistake," while Sen. Amy Klobuchar's gubernatorial campaign called a number of his past statements "reckless and unacceptable." Other Democratic officials and party groups have gone further, calling on Omar and state Sen. Omar Fateh, who is hosting the sold-out Minneapolis event, to cancel the appearance. The controversy is exposing a divide among Minnesota Democrats in the closing stretch of the midterms over whether Piker's enormous following among younger progressives outweighs the political liability of his past rhetoric. University of Minnesota political science professor Larry Jacobs told FOX 9 the event would "create a split within the DFL," arguing it could distract statewide Democrats from their closing message and put candidates in a difficult position with moderate and Jewish voters. WHO IS HASAN PIKER? MEET THE FAR-LEFT STREAMER WHO IS STIRRING UP CONTROVERSY AND DIVIDING DEMOCRATS Piker, who commands millions of followers across social media, has faced backlash over remarks involving the Sept. 11 attacks, Hamas, Israel and Jewish people. He later apologized for saying in 2019 that "America deserved 9/11" and has rejected accusations of antisemitism. Omar's campaign, however, has defended her decision to participate by pointing to Piker's appeal among the younger voters Democrats are trying to turn out ahead of Election Day. DEMOCRATS CONDEMNING HASAN PIKER AS BACKLASH SPREADS THROUGH PARTY "Early voting among people under 40 is down, and we need to do everything to get young people to the polls," Omar's campaign told FOX 9. "The Congresswoman knows the Democratic Party is a Big Tent party, and she's excited to join Senator Omar Fateh's event to mobilize young voters and get them to vote in this critical midterm election." During an appearance on "Pod Save America" earlier this year, Piker said he would "vote for Hamas over Israel every single time." He has also described Orthodox Jews as "inbred" and faced renewed criticism this summer over remarks warning that continued American Jewish support for Israel could provoke someone to "take action." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "People don't f--- with Israel any longer. And if Jews in America keep putting this idea out there that they're singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone will come around and take action not against Israel, mind you, but against American Jews," Piker said in August. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER Fox News Digital reached out to Omar's campaign, Fateh and Piker for additional comment on the mounting criticism and calls to cancel Monday night's event but did not immediately receive a response. Fox News Digital's Brian Flood and Rachel Wolf contributed to this report.

articles.title: Anti-Zionism isn’t always antisemitism, but don’t ignore the red flags
articles.summary: Haverford had previously been given fair notice that campus anti-Zionism could descend into palpable antisemitism but chose to ignore it.
articles.body:
It is certainly true that anti-Zionism and antisemitism are conceptually distinct phenomena, but that does not mean they are unrelated in reality. There has always been an undercurrent of anti-Jewish bigotry in much criticism of Israel. Sometimes, only a dramatic revelation can uncover a connection.

Consider the case of Haverford College, in suburban Philadelphia, where Jewish students, with ties of religion and shared ancestry to Israel, had complained of intimidation from classmates, administrators and faculty. The college administration insisted that the alleged harassment was not based on Jewish identity, but rather on “specific political views and positions on world events, namely, the Israel-Palestine conflict.”

Then a tenured Haverford faculty member was arrested by the FBI for repeatedly sending menacing messages to a Jewish colleague, with hate-filled slurs and embedded threats of violence. That finally prompted Haverford’s president, Wendy Raymond to officially acknowledge antisemitism at her college.

In a statement to the college community, Raymond declared that she was “heartbroken and furious” at the “heinous online attacks, which were antisemitic in nature.”

Haverford had previously been given fair notice that campus anti-Zionism could descend into palpable antisemitism but chose to ignore it.

In 2024, a group of Jewish students and faculty, calling themselves Jews at Haverford, filed a federal civil rights lawsuit against the college. Their 90-page complaint alleged numerous instances of disparate treatment, insults, shunning, exclusion and bullying from other students and faculty — based on their Jewish identification with Israel — that had been tolerated or disregarded by Haverford’s administration.

In a subsequent pleading , the plaintiffs submitted five X posts by Professor Guangtian Ha, of the Haverford religion department, comprising “abusive, obscene denunciations” of Zionism and Zionists, which would thus include “every Haverford student” who is a Zionist.

Ha declared that “the only way to deal with zionists is to stop talking to them,” and “anyone who says ‘what about Hamas’ can go f— themself.”

Ominously foreshadowing worse things to come, Ha warned that “in my little world . . I will never forgive them. I know their names and I know their faces.”

Despite the implicit threats for the exclusion, or worse, of students who care for Israel, the Haverford administration failed to investigate, reprimand or even caution Ha. Rather than recognize the glaring red flag, Haverford argued that the threatening posts, and similar alleged incidents, constituted only “opposing viewpoints on world affairs.”

Regrettably, the court agreed . In baffling disregard of Ha’s obscene condemnation of certain names and faces, whom he would never forgive in Haverford’s little world, the judge held that the posts were “leveled at the State of Israel” and therefore not aimed at “people of Jewish descent.”

But Ha then proved them both wrong. In October 2025, he allegedly began cyberstalking a Jewish professor who had drawn his ire. According to the indictment and other prosecution pleadings , Ha used multiple phony X accounts to send the victim more than 50 vicious and unmistakably threatening antisemitic messages.

The messages were filled with classically anti-Jewish images: “Jewish cockroaches,” “blood guzzling demons,” “Jew pig,” “jew filth” and “demonic evil of the jews.” They often trafficked in overt Nazi language: “The fuhrer is coming;” Jews should be “placed in special camps;” “Exterminate the jews;” “Make it 6 million;” and “you shall see a true holocaust.”

Far worse were the threats. Several messages referred to the township where the victim’s family lives: “The end of American jews is close. Let’s start with the jews in Lower Merion.”

Other messages included the address and photographs of the victim’s home, one with an “eyes” emoji and another with a bulls-eye emoji. Still others evinced real-time access to the house: “Blurring your home on google map and installing a security camera next to your mailbox won’t help.”

Most terrifying was a threatening warning against the victims’ children that included the name of the family’s seven-month-old infant. “Homeless dogs jews will once again become, if you do survive,” Ha wrote. On two occasions, the harassment was so severe that the victimized family fled their home with their three minor children.

According to the prosecution, Ha “admitted to FBI agents that he created and used” the offending accounts, which had been traced to his IP addresses. Ha has pleaded not guilty . His defense attorney did not respond to multiple inquiries from me.

Although now banned from campus, Ha had been active in Haverford’s anti-Zionist movement, once having ironically complained of “Zionist witch hunts.”

It would be foolish to argue that anti-Zionism is always camouflage for antisemitism. But as Ha’s example demonstrates, it would be dangerous to assume that it never is.

It seems improbable that Ha could have been exposed to the vile language of Western antisemitism in China, where he was born and raised . It is far more likely that he could have learned it on an American college campus, after moving here in his early twenties to attend graduate school at Columbia.

Therein lies an important lesson for university administrators. There is barely concealed bigotry lurking on your campuses. Listen to your Jewish students, who can tell you much about antisemitism if you are willing to pay attention.

Steven Lubet is the Williams Memorial Professor Emeritus at the Northwestern University Pritzker School of Law. He is the author of “The ‘Colored Hero’ of Harpers Ferry: John Anthony Copeland and the War against Slavery,” and many other books.

articles.title: House Democrats call on DOJ to name  special counsel in Epstein case
articles.summary: House Democrats call for independent special counsel to investigate evidence of alleged Trump criminal ties to Jeffrey Epstein
articles.body: WASHINGTON — House Judiciary Committee Democrats are calling for an independent special counsel to investigate evidence of President Donald Trump’s alleged criminal ties to Jeffrey Epstein, according to a new report made public Monday. “The bottom line,” they wrote in the report, “There is more than sufficient evidence to launch a criminal investigation.” They acknowledged the Justice Department under Trump would be unlikely to appoint a special counsel, — such as Robert Mueller who ran the Russia investigation or Jack Smith, who led the investigation into Trump’s efforts to overturn his 2020 election loss in the lead-up to the Jan. 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol. The president has repeatedly denied any knowledge of, or involvement in, Epstein’s criminal activity and said he cut ties well before allegations of sex trafficking by the financier became public. “None of these allegations are true. This ‘report’ is nothing more than a desperate attempt by crazed Democrats to distract Americans from the surging Republican momentum driven by President Trump’s historic achievements,” said Lauren Bis, a White House spokeswoman. “The President kicked Jeffrey Epstein out of his club at Mar-a-Lago because he was a creep.” The report comes on the brink of the midterm elections, when Democrats are hoping to seize control of Congress as the president’s approval rating tanks over the economy, affordability and the war with Iran. The report signaled an avenue of focus for lawmakers in January should Democrats win a chamber of Congress. A bipartisan law signed by Congress last November ordered the release of millions of documents related to the case against Epstein, who died by suicide in jail while awaiting federal sex trafficking and conspiracy charges. Many of America’s wealthy and powerful appear in the files, including Trump, who is mentioned thousands of times. But only one person was ever convicted, Epstein’s accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell. No one else has been charged in the United States. Right now, Democratic oversight efforts have been limited because they are in the minority in Congress, unable to compel witness testimony or solicit documents through subpoena without the help of Republicans. While the Republican-led House Oversight Committee has subpoenaed several Epstein associates and Republicans helped to pass the Epstein Transparency Act, they have been largely unwilling to look deeper into Trump’s ties to the late sex offender. Democrats’ power would change dramatically should the party win the majority back in either chamber. They would be able to issue subpoenas with or without the help of Republicans. In addition to the Epstein probe, Democratic leaders have promised robust investigations into alleged corruption and grift in Trump’s administration and family businesses. In their report released Monday, Democrats accuse the Justice Department of obstructing investigations into potential Epstein co-conspirators, including, they say, Trump. The report alleges the DOJ worked to cover up the president’s connections to Epstein, and said an independent special counsel is necessary, because Attorney General Todd Blanche, who was once Trump’s personal attorney, was compromised. “The women who survived Epstein deserve to be heard, Congress must have the complete files required by law, and an independent special counsel must investigate Epstein’s co-conspirators and DOJ’s cover-up and ensure that state and foreign prosecutors have the evidence they need to pursue justice,” Rep. Jamie Raskin of Maryland, the panel’s top Democrat, said in a statement. A Justice Department spokesperson said in a statement Monday that the report was “nothing more than a last-ditch effort by House Judiciary Democrats to mislead the public.” The department complied with the Congressional act, “making public the nearly 3 million investigatory documents which were responsive to the Act. The Department also freely offered members of Congress the opportunity to view the files unredacted. All these files were part of FBI investigations that spanned decades and these claims were investigated by agents at the time.” The Justice Department spokesperson said DOJ can’t talk about the existence of any ongoing investigations, but noted the only administration to bring federal charges against Epstein was Trump’s. The Democrats vowed to continue investigating it themselves. “Given DOJ and FBI’s abdication of their law enforcement duties and prosecutorial ethics, there is little reason to believe this administration will take even this minimal step,” according to the report. “Accordingly, Congress must continue to use its legislative and oversight powers to pursue justice for survivors and bring an end to the Trump Administration’s shameful, bureaucratic, and political cover-up.” Trump was at one point friends with Epstein. “I’ve known Jeff for 15 years. Terrific guy,” Trump told New York magazine in 2002, before there were any public allegations of wrongdoing by the financier. “He’s a lot of fun to be with,” Trump said then. “It is even said that he likes beautiful women as much as I do, and many of them are on the younger side.” Epstein pleaded guilty in 2008 in a Florida state court to felony solicitation of prostitution and procuring minors for prostitution, in a heavily-criticized plea deal. He was sentenced to 18 months, though he served about a year before he was released. He was arrested in 2019 on a federal sex trafficking conspiracy charge and one count of sex trafficking underage women. After Epstein’s arrest, Trump, who was president at the time, distanced himself from the disgraced financier. “I was not a fan,” he told reporters at a July 2019 news conference. “I had a falling out with him a long time ago.” The staff report on Epstein released Monday draws on interviews the staff conducted with witnesses, as well as files released by the Justice Department related to its investigation of Epstein.

articles.title: Trump-appointed judge slams door on DOJ as court losses pile up days ahead of midterms
articles.summary: A judge President Donald Trump appointed dismissed the DOJ's lawsuit against Utah Lt. Gov. Deidre Henderson over state voter data with prejudice.
articles.body: A federal judge appointed by President Donald Trump has handed his administration another loss in its quest to tackle alleged illegal voting ahead of the midterm elections. District Judge David Barlow on Friday dismissed a case the Department of Justice brought against Utah Lt. Gov. Deidre Henderson, a Republican, demanding that she turn over state voter data. The administration sought to compel Henderson, the state’s top election official, to hand over a complete list of Utah voters, including their names, birthdays and addresses as well as their driver's license numbers or the last four digits of their Social Security numbers. The Justice Department’s defeat in Utah is one of more than 25 voter-roll litigation defeats the Trump administration has suffered since beginning its campaign to address alleged illegal voting. "The only appellate court yet to review this has split on largely partisan grounds," a DOJ spokeswoman told Fox News Digital, noting that the department would be appealing the decision. "Five [sixth circuit] judges signed on to powerful dissents from denial of en banc review." TRUMP-APPOINTED FEDERAL JUDGE TOSSES DOJ LAWSUIT SEEKING ARIZONA VOTER DATA Federal lawyers initially sued Henderson, arguing that the Civil Rights Act of 1960 requires her to make certain voting records that "come into" her possession available for federal inspection. Barlow, however, cited a ruling from the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals that found "an ordinary English speaker would not say that she has come into possession of something that she created, established and maintained," a reference to the broad dataset the DOJ was seeking to obtain. The DOJ countered that line of argument by asserting that, even if the precise language of the law didn’t require the data to be surrendered, the purpose of the law in question was to serve as enforcement tool for federal election laws, so it would make little sense to interpret it as excluding the statewide voter-registration database that states use to carry out voter-list maintenance. FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS DOJ ACCESS TO NJ VOTER ROLLS AMID STATEWIDE CONTROVERSY Barlow rejected this line of argument, stating that judges have "no warrant to elevate vague invocations of statutory purpose over the words Congress chose." Trump tapped Barlow to serve on the federal bench in 2019. Before being nominated, Barlow served as a Republican congressional lawyer, a federal prosecutor and a private attorney. TRUMP-APPOINTED FEDERAL JUDGE RULES AGAINST ADMIN ON MAINE VOTER ROLL DATA Barlow dismissed the administration’s complaint with prejudice, meaning that the DOJ cannot simply refile the same claim, though the department can appeal the ruling to a higher court. "We appreciate Judge Barlow's ruling dismissing the Department of Justice's lawsuit that sought to force us to disclose the private data of every Utah voter," Henderson wrote on Threads. articles.title: Catholic bishops apologise for 'exploited' Trump meeting
articles.summary: Two bishops in images that show them praying with Trump have said they believed the meeting was private.
articles.body:
Two Catholic bishops in the US have said they regret meeting President Donald Trump at the White House, after images of them praying with him were released and prompted many to ask if they were making a political statement.

Photos and video of the 22 October meeting show a group of bishops standing around Trump at the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office.

Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob, one of those pictured, said he had believed the meeting was private and not "a political photo opportunity".

Trump and Pope Leo XIV have a contentious relationship, and some US bishops have criticised the White House's immigration stance. Trump won the support of 55% of Catholic voters in 2024, a Pew study found.

In a statement posted online, Bishop William Joensen of Des Moines, Iowa, said the meeting was arranged by officials with the White House Faith Office to discuss issues including immigration, visas for international clergy and the "exploitation of vulnerable poor persons".

"In no way did any of us intend by our involvement to endorse any political party or any individual candidate," Joensen said.

"I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purposes," he added.

A video of the meeting was released by Margo Martin, a special assistant to the president and communications adviser who frequently shares behind-the-scenes images of Trump on social media.

Archbishop Grob said that after 90 minutes of meetings with officials, the religious leaders were ushered into the Oval Office to pray with Trump.

Grob said images of the meeting later caused concern among some of his congregants.

"I soon began receiving messages of serious concern over the possibility that I had inadvertently participated in a political event less than two weeks before a national election," he wrote.

"I also heard from some who felt wounded because of the ways they or their family have been harmed by the president's policies," he added.

Grob said none of the participants in the meeting gave permission for the public distribution or posting of video or photos of the event.

When contacted for comment by the BBC, the White House did not directly address questions regarding the meeting or subsequent comments by the two bishops.

"There has never been a greater president for Catholic Americans than President Trump, and his strong record proves it," White House Spokeswoman Taylor Rogers said in a statement.

According to Pew Research Center, which analyses religion in the US, opinions of Trump's performance have slipped among all major religious groups. In a survey this month, 30% of all US Catholics said they approved of his job performance, compared to 47% when he returned to the White House in 2025.

That could have an effect on the 3 November midterm elections, which will decide control of Congress. More Catholics in the survey, 42%, said they preferred the Democrats running in their local House of Representatives races, where slightly less, 39% favoured Republicans.

During his second term, Trump has had a tense relationship with the head of the Catholic church, Pope Leo, as he has moved aggressively to remove people believed to be in the US illegally.

Nine days before the Oval Office meeting with the bishops took place, Bishop Brendon Cahill and Walter Kim, the president of the National Association of Evangelicals, issued a statement urging "Christian compassion and wisdom in the immigration debate".

They said the immigration clampdown has led to the "sowing of fear, the fracturing of families, the deprivation of due process, and the vilification of our neighbors."

The US Conference of Catholic Bishops also recently condemned the Trump administration's plans to livestream a military execution , which were later scrapped.

Both Vice-President JD Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are Catholics who have visited the Vatican during Trump's second term.

A Midwestern member of the bishops' conference, Robert Barron of Minnesota, agreed to serve on the president's Religious Liberty Commission last year, as did former New York Archbishop Timothy Dolan.

articles.title: The 2026 midterms are just 8 days away. Which party has a better chance of winning? Here's what the latest polls say.
articles.summary: Trump's approval rating is going down. Democrats' lead on the generic ballot is going up. Could this be a "wave" election?
articles.body:
The 2026 midterm elections are just 8 days away. So where do things stand — nationwide — in the race to control Congress? Which party has a better chance of, you know, winning? To get a sense of that, it helps to geek out over some cold, hard data.

The usual caveats apply, of course. Polls aren't predictions; they're momentary snapshots of public opinion. Big events can, and often do, change the course of elections. And polls have been wrong before .

Yet time is running out — and the stakes in November couldn't be higher, especially for President Trump, who has enjoyed complete Republican control of Congress for the first half of his second term. Flipping the House would give Democrats the power to block the president's agenda, investigate his administration and even impeach him (again); flipping the Senate would allow them to stymie his Supreme Court nominees too.

The state-by-state midterm landscape is finally firming up — and some clear polling trends are emerging. Here are the numbers to watch as Election Day nears.

Every pollster asks a version of the same question: If an election for U.S. Congress were held today, which party's candidate would you vote for in your district? In fact, this particular polling prompt is so pervasive, it's known as the "generic ballot" (at least among politics nerds).

You obviously can't divine the outcome of an entire midterm election from a single question that flattens 435 House contests into a binary choice between "the Democrat" and "the Republican." But the generic ballot can suggest which direction voters are heading.

At this point in 2022 — after more than a year and a half of Democratic President Joe Biden and Democratic majorities in the House and Senate — Republicans had a small but significant lead (2.7 percentage points) on the generic ballot. On Election Day, the GOP translated its final polling lead of 3 percentage points into nine seats — enough to flip the House.

At this point in 2018 — with Trump as president and Republican majorities in the House and Senate — Democrats were leading by an average of 7.6 points on the generic ballot. Eight days later, they picked up 41 seats and flipped the House.

Polarization wasn't as extreme in 2014 and 2010, the two midterms under Democratic President Barack Obama; minds weren't made up quite so early. But with 8 days to go, voters had clearly broken against Democrats. In 2014, a Republican polling lead of 3.1 points translated into a net gain of 13 seats in the House; in 2010, those numbers were 6.9 points and 63 seats, respectively.

So what does that mean for 2026? Historically speaking, a president's party almost always loses seats when voters return to the polls to judge his first two years in office. Sometimes, the backlash is so pervasive that the president's party loses pretty much every close-ish contest — a phenomenon known as a "wave" election.

Right now, Democrats have a wave-sized lead on the generic ballot — about 9 percentage points , on average — and it has grown over the last month.

Democrats might not reprise 2018 and flip 41 House seats again in November, in part because red-state Republican lawmakers have recently redrawn congressional maps across the South to benefit their party in ways that blue-state Democrats have been unable to keep up with . But they only need to pick up three seats to win back the House.

National dynamics tend to define the composition of the incoming House. But Senate contests are quirkier — more state-specific and personality-driven. Democrats currently hold 47 Senate seats; they'd need 51 to control the chamber. (A 50-50 split would give Vice President JD Vance the tiebreaking vote). Polls suggest that flipping four Republican seats is very possible. In the states where Dems are playing defense — Michigan, Georgia, New Hampshire — their leads are solidifying; meanwhile, red states such as Iowa, Kansas, Nebraska and South Carolina seem increasingly competitive. Here are the 12 races to follow:

What the latest polls say : Jackson, who replaced Graham Platner , the Democrats' previous scandal-plagued nominee, tends to lead Collins by anywhere from 2 to 4 percentage points . The most recent nonpartisan poll — a Fox News survey released on Thursday — shows a tie, and a Republican poll released over the weekend gives Collins a 0.5% edge.

Republican Mike Rogers (former member of Congress)

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed (public-health epidemiologist and former Wayne County, Mich. health director)

What the latest polls say : Nineteen polls have been conducted over the last month. Eighteen of them showed El-Sayed in the lead, by anywhere from 1 to 7 percentage points .

What the latest polls say : All but one poll conducted over the last month shows Brown edging Husted , with margins ranging from 1 to 8 percentage points.

Republican Mike Collins (member of Congress)

What the latest polls say : Ossoff holds a solid lead over Collins, with October polls putting him ahead by an average of 8 percentage points .

Republican Michael Whatley (former Republican National Committee chairman)

What the latest polls say : Cooper leads by more than 10 points, on average . One of the most recent nonpartisan surveys showed him ahead by 14 .

What the latest polls say : Pappas and Sununu were previously trading leads in polls in the race to replace retiring Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen. But Pappas appears to have opened a substantial lead — average margin: 7 percentage points — over the last month.

Democrat Mary Peltola (former member of Congress)

What the latest polls say : Surveys conducted in October show Peltola leading by anywhere from 2 to 7 percentage points . Some September polls showed a tie, or Sullivan slightly ahead.

Republican Ashley Hinson (member of Congress)

Democrat Josh Turek (state legislator and former Paralympic athlete)

What the latest polls say : Hinson and Turek have traded small leads in surveys released since Iowa's June 2 primaries .

Republican Ken Paxton (state attorney general)

Democrat James Talarico (state legislator)

What the latest polls say : Nearly every poll conducted over this fall has shown Talarico leading Paxton, though the margins are small — between 2 and 6 points.

Independent Dan Osborn (veteran and former union leader with Democratic support)

What the latest polls say : Surveys are few and far between. But the most recent nonpartisan results suggest Osborn could be competitive, and a couple of new Osborn-affiliated polls show Ricketts and his independent challenger trading small leads.

Democrat Adam Hamilton (Methodist pastor who previously considered an independent run)

What the latest polls say : Marshall leads by 1 point in the latest sounding — but it's the only survey conducted over the last month that shows him ahead. The rest (save one tie) give Hamilton a slight edge (between 1 and 5 percentage points).

Republican Darline Graham (incumbent, appointed to replace her brother Lindsey Graham after his death in July)

Democrat Annie Andrews (pediatrician and former U.S. House candidate)

What the latest polls say : Graham holds a narrow lead in recent surveys . But it is small enough — between 1 and 3 percentage points — that Democrats are now targeting South Carolina as well. A partisan poll released on Thursday gave Andrews a 1-point advantage.

Advantage? Democrats. They've been consistently gaining ground over the last month, to the point where they are now favored to flip the Senate — unless the polls are wrong.

Trump's approval rating — especially on affordability

To one degree or another, midterm elections are always referendums on how the president is performing. So Trump is the final piece of the puzzle.

At the moment, that's unfortunate news for Republicans on Capitol Hill and those looking to join them.

According to the data journalists at Silver Bulletin , 60.2% of Americans, on average, currently disapprove of how Trump is handling his job vs. 36.9% who approve. That puts the president's net approval rating at -23.3% — near his all-time low.

Here's a sampling of Trump's latest net approval numbers from a few top pollsters:

Again, history can provide perspective . In late-October 2018, Trump was about 10 points "underwater"; Republicans went on to lose 41 seats that November.

According to the New York Times , Trump has the second lowest approval rating heading into the midterms since 1946, behind only Harry Truman. George W. Bush's approval rating was higher at this point in 2006 — a year in which Democrats went on to flip the House and Senate.

Trump is earning even lower marks on voters' top 2026 issue: the cost of living . Shortly after he returned to office, roughly equal numbers of Americans approved and disapproved of how the president was handling inflation. But today, 71% disapprove and 25% approve. That's a 46-point gap.

In comparison, Biden's approval rating on inflation was rarely underwater by more than 30 points during his presidency — a period that coincided with the economic shocks of COVID-19 and ended with him choosing not to stand for reelection.

articles.title: Ramaswamy humanized his opponent and dehumanized himself
articles.summary: Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy’s attempt to discredit Ohio gubernatorial opponent Dr. Amy Acton via an advertisement featuring her mother’s testimony backfired, instead highlighting Acton’s resilience in overcoming childhood trauma.
articles.body:
October surprises are nothing new and are now to be expected. Every time a news story breaks the October before the election, people try to tie it to said election whether it really matters or not. Osama Bin Laden made an appearance in 2004 . The “Access Hollywood” tape. The James Comey investigation . Heck, even the rioting in France is being looked at as one that would help the Republicans as they look to prevent a bloodbath at the ballots.

But Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, in his effort to slander his Ohio gubernatorial adversary Amy Acton (D), instead committed the cardinal sin of politics. He completely humanized her.

Ramaswamy released an ad in which Acton’s mother said she was not to be trusted, lied about her youth, and lied about the hardships she faced. I have racked my memory and could not think of a time when a politician’s own mother spoke out against him or her. The closest I could get was Pete Hegseth’s mother’s emails , from which she later walked back.

Now if you asked me what I knew about Acton before this past week, I would have told you that she was a doctor, she came to prominence during COVID and that she was a Democrat. That’s it. I have a sneaking suspicion that anyone outside of Ohio who wasn’t an ardent politico would probably have known just as little.

But this week, I learned that she endured the unendurable as a child. She went through a trauma that no human should ever go through and she protected her brother in the process. I learned that her abuser was a man who lived in her house and was married to her mother. That alone would be devastating to deal with, but it gets worse.

The one person who should have protected her and believed her turned out to be her worst enemy. Her own mother sided with the man who was charged with raping her . Even with an indictment and with him fleeing justice, she stuck by his side until his death. Acton and her brother understandably cut off contact with her.

We know that victims of child sexual abuse can struggle to live the lives they deserve to. Many turn to drugs or alcohol. Many deal with depression and thoughts of suicide. Some turn to partners who mistreat them. It is not easy to build a good life for yourself after you have been abused, especially when that abuse is coupled with the betrayal by your own mother.

But, thanks to Ramaswamy, I learned that she chose to rise up. She paid her way through college , went to medical school, got a masters from my alma mater Ohio State and then spent her adult life helping people.

We are accustomed to politicians trying to paint their opponents as “others.” They are the enemy, they don’t have anything in common with you and will not work in your interests. That is the reason politicians call people socialists, fascists or communists. They paint them as billionaires, rich, or beholden to those with wealth. They attack their religion by calling them Muslims or Zionists. They try like hell to put a gap between you and their opponent.

We saw a viral moment this week when a heckler (political operative) named Tommy decided to “other” Michigan senatorial candidate Abdul El-Sayed by asking him to denounce the Muslim Brotherhood. El-Sayed did and then gave an eloquent speech about the Constitution, freedom of religion, and likened himself to John F. Kennedy. In an effort to make El-Sayed look like an outsider, Tommy succeeded in having voters learn just how eloquent and patriotic he was.

Tommy might not have expected that, but Ramaswamy should have a million times over before he decided to defend his attack ad. For a party that claims to care about children, the GOP has already struggled to deal with the fallout of the Epstein files to Ohio Republican Rep. Max Miller’s abuse allegations . Why do these things matter? In the United States alone , one in four girls and one in 13 boys experience child sexual abuse. It means that many people will unfortunately share the same experience as Amy Acton.

Ramaswamy, backed by President Trump and Vice President JD Vance, didn’t show any contrition. In this era of MAGA masculinity, admitting you were wrong or showing empathy to your opponents seems to be unmanly. But any decent person sees his behavior (and those defending it) as inhumane.

Ramaswamy may survive this blunder; the polls show a very tight race. But his campaign’s race to the bottom shows a very deep flaw in his character. He is known as a brilliant man who made a lot of money at a very young age. But he showed that he has no understanding of trauma, overcoming adversity or empathy. If he had, he would not have made his opponent look like the strong person that he turned out not to be.

Joslin Joseph is a recipient of the Military Reporters and Editors award for Best Commentary-Opinion. A graduate of Harvard and Ohio State, he is a Marine veteran who served in Iraq. He currently lives in Anaheim, Calif.

articles.title: Former diplomats, top foreign affairs experts back Jackson in Maine Senate race
articles.summary: More than 60 former diplomats and top foreign affairs experts are backing Democrat Troy Jackson as he vies for a Maine Senate seat next week against Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine). Sixty-two officials — including former U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Susan Rice, former Deputy Secretary of State Wendy Sherman, former Undersecretary of State for…
articles.body:
More than 60 former diplomats and top foreign affairs experts are backing Democrat Troy Jackson as he vies for a Maine Senate seat next week against Sen. Susan Collins (R-Maine).

Sixty-two officials — including former U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Susan Rice, former Deputy Secretary of State Wendy Sherman, former Undersecretary of State for Political Affairs Thomas Pickering and former Director General of Foreign Service W. Robert Pearson — signed a letter throwing their support behind the former Maine Senate president’s candidacy, which was released Monday and first shared with The Hill.

The letter, whose signatories span appointees from former President Carter to President Trump and many of whom Collins voted to confirm, rebuked the GOP senator over her voting record and laid blame with her for the war with Iran and the tariff war with Canada.

“Maine’s Senate election could determine whether Donald Trump’s party controls the Senate for the next two years. Our country needs a Senate willing to check presidential abuses, confront corruption, and challenge a reckless foreign policy that punishes our allies while emboldening our adversaries,” the letter said.

“The most consequential thing Susan Collins does in the U.S. Senate is enable Donald Trump. She paints herself as a moderate while voting with Trump 96% of the time,” the letter added. “Her occasional breaks mean little when Republicans already have the votes they need.”

A CQ Roll Call analysis shows the GOP senator has voted with the president 92 percent of the time during Trump’s second term and 90 percent of the time during Trump’s first term.

The letter criticized Collins for voting against multiple war powers resolutions aimed at reining in Trump’s ability to go to war with Iran and for voting “to confirm the officials charged with carrying out Trump’s tariff agenda despite their stated intentions.”

The letter, meanwhile, applauded Jackson for protecting abortion access — an area where his positions have evolved since he got his start in politics — and tackling healthcare costs.

“He brings the judgment of someone who knows what it means to work for a living, listens to his neighbors, and delivers for the people he represents,” the letter added.

Collins campaign spokesperson Blake Kernen responded to the letter, telling The Hill in a statement that he was “touting other people’s foreign policy credentials because he lacks experience and expertise of his own.”

“No endorsement letter can substitute for not knowing the basics of foreign policy. CNN’s Dana Bash had to correct Troy Jackson’s claim that Iran controlled the Strait of Hormuz before the war,” Kernen added, referring to an interview Jackson did with the network earlier this month . “He has accused the Israeli government of ‘genocide’ and pledged never to vote for U.S. military aid to our ally. Mainers deserve a senator who understands the stakes.”

Jackson and Collins are in a tight match for next week’s election, with a polling average of Maine Senate surveys compiled by Decision Desk HQ showing the Democrat barely ahead at 49 percent support to her 48 percent.

Collins has positioned herself as a moderate Republican who has rankled her party and Trump by breaking with them on certain issues. While Collins did vote against some war power resolutions regarding the Iran war, she joined one other GOP senator in April to vote in favor of a war powers resolution. In September, she and several other Senate Republicans broke ranks and voted in favor of a resolution pressing Trump to end the Iran war, though it failed in the upper chamber.

“As I have said since these hostilities began, the President’s authority as Commander-in-Chief is not without limits,” Collins said in a statement at the time. “The Constitution gives Congress an essential role in decisions of war and peace, and the War Powers Act establishes a clear 60-day deadline for Congress to either authorize or end U.S. involvement in foreign hostilities. That deadline is not a suggestion; it is a requirement.”

Collins, who has voted to confirm officials like U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, has also broken with the Trump administration on the tariff war with Canada, of which Maine borders and does trade with.

The GOP senator announced last week that she had secured trade exemptions for certain categories of products that are vital to Maine’s agricultural industry.
